subtitle: In the yellow gorge of Mewar, a battle is fought twice—once with steel, and forever in memory.

panels.shot: wide, dramatic split composition, one half a rocky yellow pass with Maharana Pratap poised to charge, the other half a disciplined Mughal-Rajput host under Man Singh I
panels.action: Maharana Pratap, stern and unbent in Rajput armour on Chetak, faces across a hazy, dust-choked valley toward Man Singh I, calm and watchful in Mughal-Rajput battle array atop an armoured war-elephant, the Haldighati hills glowing a mustard yellow under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: On 18 June 1576, in the yellow gorge of Haldighati, Maharana Pratap and Man Singh I crossed steel—and left behind a battle whose very story the chroniclers could not agree upon.

i18n.hi: १८ जून १५७६ को, हल्दीघाटी की पीली घाटी में, महाराणा प्रताप और मान सिंह ने तलवारें भिड़ाईं—और पीछे ऐसी जंग छोड़ गए, जिसकी कहानी पर ही इतिहासनिगार न झट पाये।

panels.shot: slow push-in over a bird’s-eye of Chittor’s broken walls and smouldering towers
panels.action: The ruined bastions of Chittor Fort rise over the plains, towers cracked, gateways blackened, siege ramps abandoned, the stone scarred by cannon fire under a smoky sky.

dialogue.text: Three years before Haldighati, in 1568, Akbar’s guns broke Chittor. Mewar’s ancient capital fell, but its ruler, Maharana Pratap, was not there to bend his knee.

i18n.hi: हल्दीघाटी से तीन साल पहले, १५६८ में, अकबर की तोपों ने चित्तौड़ तोड़ दिया। मेवाड़ की प्राचीन राजधानी गिर गई, पर उसका राणा, महाराणा प्रताप, घुटने टेकने वहाँ मौजूद ही नहीं था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Maharana Pratap in a rocky forest camp, contrasted in the background with a court scene of Akbar and Man Singh
panels.action: In a scrubby Aravalli camp, Maharana Pratap, rugged and bareheaded, studies a rough map by firelight, while in a faded, ghostlike background panel, Akbar seats Man Singh I in honour at the Mughal court, hand resting on the Rajput prince’s shoulder.

dialogue.text: Pratap refused submission and took to the hills. As he gathered scattered clans and Bhil allies, Akbar raised other Rajputs to high rank—among them Man Singh of Amber, soon his most trusted general.

i18n.hi: प्रताप ने सिर झुकाने से इंकार किया और पहाड़ों का रूख किया। वह बिखरे कुलों और भील साथियों को जोड़ता रहा, उधर अकबर ने दूसरे राजपूतों को ऊँचे ओहदों पर चढ़ाया—उनमें आमेर के मान सिंह भी थे, जो जल्द ही उसका सबसे भरोसेमंद सेनापति बन गया।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot of Rajasthan with arrows and banners marking Mewar and Mughal fronts
panels.action: A stylised map of western India shows Mewar’s rugged hills marked with Pratap’s sun-banner, while from Agra and Ajmer, lines of Mughal standards and Rajput emblems move toward the Aravallis, converging near Gogunda and Haldighati.

dialogue.text: By 1576 the frontier hardened. Mughal garrisons spread through Rajasthan, yet Mewar’s heartland held out. Akbar ordered Man Singh to break this last Rajput kingdom that still stood wholly outside his empire.

i18n.hi: १५७६ आते-आते सरहद सख्त हो गई। मुग़ल छावनियाँ राजस्थान में फैल गईं, पर मेवाड़ का दिल अब भी अडिग रहा। अकबर ने मान सिंह को हुक्म दिया कि इस आख़िरी राजपूत रियासत को तोड़ो, जो अभी तक पूरी की पूरी उसके साम्राज्य से बाहर खड़ी थी।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Haldighati pass from a high vantage, showing its narrow, twisting path
panels.action: The Haldighati pass winds like a pale yellow scar between steep, scrub-covered ridges; tiny figures of armoured riders and light-footed men move to occupy rocky spurs and gullies.

dialogue.text: They met in the Haldighati gorge near Gogunda, the soil stained yellow by its stone. Here a small force could bite into a larger host, if the hills and dust were used well.

i18n.hi: वे गोगुन्दा के पास हल्दीघाटी की सँकरी घाटी में मिले, जहाँ मिट्टी खुद पत्थर की पीली धूल से रंगी थी। यहाँ छोटी टुकड़ी भी बड़ी फौज को काट सकती थी—अगर पहाड़ और धूल को सही खेला जाए।

panels.shot: tight, ground-level shot of Pratap’s gathered warriors, Bhil archers in the rocks, horsemen in the pass
panels.action: Maharana Pratap, in full mail and helmet, rides along a line of Rajput horsemen crowded into the narrow path, while lean Bhil archers crouch above among rocks and thorny shrubs, bows strung and eyes sharp.

dialogue.text: Badayuni, a Mughal scholar forced into the campaign, later wrote that Pratap held barely three thousand horse and some hundreds of Bhil archers. Later tales would swell these numbers, but he saw the line with his own eyes.

i18n.hi: मजबूरन मुग़ल मुहिम में घसीटे गए विद्वान बदायूँनी ने लिखा कि प्रताप के पास मुश्किल से तीन हज़ार घुड़सवार और कुछ सौ भील तीरंदाज़ थे। बाद की कहानियाँ इन गिनतियों को फुला देंगी, पर उसने अपनी आँखों से वही पंक्ति देखी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Badayuni as a ghostly observer at the edge of a mustering Mughal-Rajput army
panels.action: A bearded Badayuni stands uneasy at the flank of a vast, ordered Mughal-Rajput host, elephants and cavalry assembling; his figure is shaded, half apart from the armoured ranks, as if more scribe than soldier.

dialogue.text: Abdul Qadir Badayuni disliked Akbar’s ways, yet fought in his army. His Muntakhab ut-Tawarikh gives our only first-hand account of Haldighati—sharp, bitter, and always careful to show his own distaste.

i18n.hi: अब्दुल कादिर बदायूँनी अकबर के तौर-तरीकों को नापसंद करता था, पर उसकी फौज में ही लड़ता रहा। उसकी ‘मुन्तखब-उत-तवारिख’ हमें हल्दीघाटी का इकलौता आँखों देखा हाल देती है—तेज, कड़वा, और हर पन्ने पर अपनी बेदिली साफ जताते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Man Singh atop an armoured elephant, the Mughal-Rajput army fanning out behind
panels.action: Man Singh I, in Mughal-style armour with Rajput ornaments, stands steady on the howdah of a richly caparisoned elephant; behind him stretch disciplined cavalry lines with both Persianate and Rajput banners fluttering.

dialogue.text: Man Singh’s army mixed Mughal veterans and Rajput contingents loyal to Akbar. Abul Fazl and Nizamuddin Ahmad praise its strength and order, built to grind down resistance rather than chase glory.

i18n.hi: मान सिंह की सेना में पुराने मुग़ल जाँबाज़ और अकबर-निष्ठ राजपूत दोनों थे। अबुल फ़ज़्ल और निज़ामुद्दीन अहमद उसकी ताकत और अनुशासन का बखान करते हैं—ऐसी फौज, जो विरोध को घिसकर खत्म करने को बनी थी, न कि बस नाम कमाने को।

panels.shot: intense split close-up: Pratap tightening his gauntlet on Chetak, Man Singh adjusting his turban-cloth on the elephant
panels.action: On one side Maharana Pratap, jaw clenched, pulls on his gauntlet while Chetak tosses his head; on the other Man Singh calmly smooths the end of his turban, eyes narrowed toward the gorge ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Maharana Pratap & Man Singh I
dialogue.text: “Today we fight not only for land,” each man thinks, “but for what it means to yield.”

i18n.hi: “आज लड़ाई सिर्फ ज़मीन की नहीं,” हर दिल में ख्याल कौंधा, “झुकने का मतलब क्या होगा, उसकी भी है।”

panels.shot: explosive wide shot of Pratap’s charge smashing into the Mughal advance at the mouth of the pass
panels.action: Pratap leads a dense wedge of Rajput horse out of the gorge, lances levelled, smashing into the front ranks of the Mughal advance; in the distance, Man Singh’s elephant turns toward the shock.

dialogue.text: When the drums finally broke the morning, Pratap did not wait. He drove straight at the van, using the narrow throat of Haldighati to blunt the advantage of numbers.

i18n.hi: जब नगाड़ों ने आखिर सन्नाटा तोड़ा, प्रताप ने देर न की। वह सीधे अगुवानी दस्ते पर टूट पड़ा, हल्दीघाटी की सँकरी ‘गरदन’ का सहारा लेकर दुश्मन की बड़ी गिनती के जोर को कुंद कर दिया।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-level shot of intermingled Rajput horse, Mughal cavalry, and Bhil archers loosing from the slopes
panels.action: The battlefield swirls as Rajput horsemen clash with Mughal cavalry, dust rising; above, Bhil archers loose arrows down into the press, their silhouettes sharp against the bright sky.

dialogue.text: Badayuni records the Bhil arrows and the sudden fury of Pratap’s charge. From the slopes, shafts hissed into men and horses; in the pass, steel and hooves tangled in choking dust.

i18n.hi: बदायूँनी भील तीरों की मार और प्रताप के धावे की अचानकता दर्ज करता है। ढालों से, ढलानों से तीरों की सिसकारी घोड़ों और सवारों को चीरती गई; दर्रे के भीतर लोहा, खुर और धूल एक घुटन भरे भंवर में उलझ गए।

panels.shot: close, tense shot of Badayuni firing while flanked by Rajput allies in Mughal service and Rajput foes
panels.action: Badayuni draws his bow amid the confusion, one side of him lined with Rajputs in Mughal service, the other with Rajput opponents surging toward them, his face twisted in conflicted focus.

dialogue.text: He wrote, with bitter irony, that he found himself shooting at Rajputs on both sides. In his telling, Haldighati was not a neat clash of ‘Mughal’ and ‘Rajput’, but kin and clans divided by policy.

i18n.hi: उसने तंज के साथ लिखा कि वह खुद दोनों तरफ के राजपूतों पर तीर चला रहा था। उसके बयान में हल्दीघाटी कोई साफ ‘मुग़ल बनाम राजपूत’ की लड़ाई नहीं, बल्कि नीतियों से बँटी हुई ख़ून-रिश्तों और कुलों की जंग थी।

panels.shot: dynamic medium shot of Man Singh signalling from his elephant as his lines begin to envelop Pratap’s force
panels.action: Amid the dust, Man Singh leans forward from his elephant howdah, arm raised, directing flanking cavalry to sweep around the struggling Rajput wedge pressing out of the pass.

dialogue.text: As the first shock passed, the larger host steadied. Abul Fazl and Nizamuddin Ahmad describe how Mughal-Rajput reserves moved to envelop Pratap’s hard-charging centre, forcing him back toward the gorge.

i18n.hi: पहला टकराव थमता ही बड़ी फौज सँभल गई। अबुल फ़ज़्ल और निज़ामुद्दीन अहमद बताते हैं कैसे मुग़ल-राजपूत रिज़र्व टुकड़ियाँ प्रताप के धावा-मार केंद्र को घेरने बढ़ीं, उसे फिर घाटी की ओर धकेलते हुए।

panels.shot: tight, dramatic shot of Pratap in the melee, Chetak rearing as he struggles to break free with a small guard
panels.action: Surrounded by turmoil, Pratap, visor lifted, urges Chetak through a gap as loyal horsemen close in around him, their faces set with desperate resolve, enemy riders pressing on every side.

dialogue.text: Later romance would weave in miracles and impossible leaps. The chroniclers agree on something plainer: pressed hard, Pratap cut his way clear with a core of followers and vanished into the broken hills.

i18n.hi: बाद की कहानियों ने चमत्कार और नामुमकिन छलाँगें जोड़ दीं। इतिहासनिगारों की बात सरल है: दबाव में घिरते हुए भी, प्रताप ने अपने चुने संगियों के साथ काटकर राह निकाली और टूटी-पहाड़ी इलाकों में गुम हो गया।

panels.shot: broad, aftermath wide shot of the battlefield with Mughal-Rajput forces holding the open field, smoke and dust settling
panels.action: Under a lowering sun, Man Singh’s troops stand in control of the trampled field, elephants and banners still; scattered weapons and fallen standards lie between them and the empty mouth of the pass leading into the hills.

dialogue.text: On one point the sources meet: Man Singh’s army held the field when fighting ebbed, and Maharana Pratap was gone. Neither Badauni nor Abul Fazl give us precise numbers, but both speak of heavy loss and exhaustion.

i18n.hi: एक बात पर सब बयान मिलते हैं: जब जंग थमी, मैदान मान सिंह की फौज के हाथ था, और महाराणा प्रताप कहीं न थे। न बदायूँनी न अबुल फ़ज़्ल ने ठीक गिनतियाँ दीं, पर दोनों भारी जानी नुक़सान और थकावट का ज़िक्र करते हैं।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Man Singh receiving a report, his face thoughtful rather than triumphant
panels.action: Man Singh sits upon his elephant in the quieted field, listening to an officer’s bowed report; his expression is controlled, composed, with no exultant smile, only measured concern.

dialogue.text: In the Mughal camp the battle was reported as a victory. Yet one question remained: the Rana lived. Later writers note Akbar’s displeasure that Man Singh, for all his discipline, had not brought Pratap bound to court.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल डेरा इसे फतह मानकर खबर भेजा। पर एक सवाल बाकी रहा: राणा जिंदा था। बाद के लेखक अकबर की नाराज़गी लिखते हैं कि मान सिंह ने, इतनी अनुशासित फौज के बावजूद, प्रताप को जकड़कर दरबार तक न ला सका।

panels.shot: intimate, low-lit shot of Pratap in a cave or remote hut with family and followers, bruised but unbowed
panels.action: In a dim hillside shelter, Pratap sits with his armour loosened, face shadowed but steady, as family members and weathered retainers gather close; a Bhil elder stands at the entrance, watching the night outside.

dialogue.text: For Pratap and his people, survival itself was a kind of victory. Haldighati did not end Mewar’s resistance; from forest hamlets and hill forts, he rebuilt, raiding and reclaiming until he could return to plains and fields.

i18n.hi: प्रताप और उसके लोगों के लिए खुद बच जाना ही एक किस्म की जीत थी। हल्दीघाटी ने मेवाड़ की प्रतिरोध-लकीर नहीं तोड़ी; जंगल-बस्तियों और पहाड़ी किलों से वह फिर उठा, धावे मारता, जमीन लौटाता, जब तक कि फिर से मैदानी खेतों की राह पकड़ सका।

panels.shot: montage-style shot: an old Rajasthani bard reciting to villagers, overlaid with faint images of the battle retold larger than life
panels.action: An elderly bard in a village courtyard raises his hand mid-recital before an entranced crowd, while behind him faint, heroic visions of Pratap loom—giant charges, rearing horses, swarming hosts—clearly grander than the earlier battle scenes.

dialogue.text: Over centuries, oral epics and later colonial romance swelled Haldighati’s scale. Armies grew in the telling, charges became legend, and the hard, narrow fight in a yellow pass turned into a timeless saga of defiance.

i18n.hi: सदियों में लोक-काव्यों और आगे चलकर अंग्रेज़ी दौर की रोमांटिक कहानियों ने हल्दीघाटी को फुलाकर बताया। फौजें बढ़ती गईं, धावे दंतकथाएँ बने, और पीली घाटी की सख्त, सँकरी जंग एक अमर विद्रोही महागाथा में बदल गई।

panels.shot: quiet, reflective split shot: a modern scholar reading Badauni and Abul Fazl, alongside spectral images of Pratap and Man Singh fading into the hills and field
panels.action: A present-day historian sits at a desk piled with Persian manuscripts, reading by lamplight, while behind her transparent figures of Maharana Pratap ride deeper into the Aravalli hills and Man Singh’s ordered ranks stand in the muted field.

dialogue.text: The chronicles agree: tactically, the field was Man Singh’s; in memory, the struggle is Pratap’s. At Haldighati, we see how battles are fought once with men and terrain, and forever after with pen, song and choice.

i18n.hi: इतिहास की किताबें मानती हैं: रणनीतिक तौर पर मैदान मान सिंह का था; यादों में संघर्ष प्रताप का। हल्दीघाटी दिखाती है कि जंग एक बार मर्दों और ज़मीन से लड़ी जाती है—और फिर हमेशा के लिए कलम, गीत और हमारी पसंदों से।

subtitle_i18n.en: In the yellow gorge of Mewar, a battle is fought twice—once with steel, and forever in memory.
subtitle_i18n.hi: मेवाड़ की पीली घाटी में, जंग दो बार लड़ी गई—एक बार हथियारों से, और हमेशा यादों में।
